items.title: DAR-Boost: A Differentiable and Adaptive Raw Data Augmentation Framework for Robust Anti-Spoofing
items.authors: Yingdong Li(Sun Yat-sen University); Chengxin Chen(China Mobile Communications Corporation); Nanli Zeng(China Mobile Communications Corporation); Jianguo Hu(Sun Yat-sen University); Kun Zeng(Sun Yat-sen University)
items.abstract: Audio deepfake detection systems face significant challenges in generalizing to unseen attacks and diverse acoustic environments. While raw waveform augmentation methods like RawBoost show promise by modeling recording noise, they rely on static parameters tailored for speech. This rigidity limits effectiveness in non-speech domains like environmental sounds. To address this, we propose DAR-Boost, an end-to-end differentiable augmentation framework. We reformulate traditional convolutive, impulsive, and stationary noise injections as fully differentiable layers governed by a lightweight auxiliary network. This network dynamically predicts optimal parameters based on the input waveform, enabling adaptive learning from the data distribution. Experimental results demonstrate that while DAR-Boost maintains comparable performance to RawBoost in the voice domain, it exhibits superior performance in the environmental sound domain, effectively broadening the framework's applicability.

items.title: Quantizer-Aware Hierarchical Neural Codec Modeling for Speech Deepfake Detection
items.authors: Jinyang Wu(A*STAR); Zihan Pan(A*STAR); Qiquan Zhang(UNSW); Sailor Hardik(A*STAR); Soumik Mondal(A*STAR)
items.abstract: Neural audio codecs discretize speech via residual vector quantization (RVQ), forming a coarse-to-fine hierarchy across quantizers. While codec models have been explored for representation learning, their discrete structure remains underutilized in speech deepfake detection. In particular, different quantization levels capture complementary acoustic cues, where early quantizers encode coarse structure and later quantizers refine residual details that reveal synthesis artifacts. Existing systems either rely on continuous encoder features or ignore this quantizer-level hierarchy. We propose a hierarchy-aware representation learning framework that models quantizer-level contributions through learnable global weighting, enabling structured codec representations aligned with forensic cues. Keeping the speech encoder backbone frozen and updating only 4.4% additional parameters, our method achieves relative EER reductions of 46.2% on ASVspoof 2019 and 13.9% on ASVspoof5 over strong baselines.

items.title: VoxENES 2026: Benchmarking Generalization of Speech Spoofing Detectors Against LLM-Era TTS and Voice Conversion
items.authors: Aastha Sharma(University of South Florida); Guangjing Wang(University of South Florida)
items.abstract: Modern LLM-driven text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC) systems produce synthetic speech that differs from the generators represented in many legacy spoofing benchmarks. This mismatch creates a temporal generalization gap that can overestimate detector robustness under real-world post-processing conditions. We bridge this gap by introducing Vox-ENES 2026, a bilingual (English and Spanish) benchmark of 53,628 audio samples generated using 10 contemporary speech synthesis methods and evaluated under 10 standardized post-processing conditions. Using VoxENES 2026, we benchmark eight pretrained detectors without fine-tuning and observe substantial performance degradation: the best model achieves 28.98% EER overall, while most perform near or below random chance across modern generators and perturbations. Our results highlight the reliance on brittle artifacts in current detectors and establish VoxENES 2026 as a practical testbed for developing robust audio spoofing countermeasures.

items.title: Soft-Gating Score-Level Fusion for Spoofing-Aware Speaker Verification
items.authors: Seongkyu Han(Soongsil University); Yowon Lee(Soongsil University); Thien An Nguyen(Soongsil University); Thien Phuc Doan(Soongsil University); Souhwan Jung(Soongsil University)
items.abstract: In Spoofing-Aware Speaker Verification (SASV), combining Automatic Speaker Verification (ASV) and Countermeasure (CM) subsystems is a key challenge. Existing approaches mainly rely on static fusion schemes, which fail to fully reflect the complementary strengths of the two subsystems. To address this limitation, we propose a Soft Gating Score-Level Fusion method that dynamically adjusts subsystem contributions based on confidence. This trial-wise adjustment allows the subsystem with higher confidence to contribute more strongly to the final decision. The proposed method requires no additional training and can be directly applied to existing SASV pipelines. Experiments on two benchmark datasets under multiple model configurations show that the proposed method achieves up to 90% relative improvement in a-DCF compared to baselines. We further analyze the conditions under which the proposed fusion is most effective, providing practical insights for stable SASV deployment.

items.title: GradHarmony: A Gradient Alignment and Magnitude Normalization Strategy for Audio Deepfake Detection
items.authors: Inho Kim(soongsil University); Thien-Phuc Doan(soongsil University); Souhwan Jung(soongsil University)
items.abstract: In audio deepfake detection, data augmentation improves model generalization by exposing them to diverse data variations. However, gradients computed from clean and augmented samples may become directionally misaligned and differ in magnitude. These discrepancies may be amplified in multi-augmentation settings, leading to unstable optimization. In this paper, we propose GradHarmony, a gradient alignment and magnitude normalization strategy for stable multi-augmentation training. GradHarmony computes gradients separately for clean data and each augmentation type, and aligns conflicting augmented gradients using the clean gradient as a reference. Then adaptively normalizes their magnitudes using exponential moving average (EMA)-based statistics to prevent dominance. Experimental results show performance improvements across a variety of models, with two state-of-the-art models achieving an average 22% reduction in equal error rate compared to the baseline on out-of-domain datasets.

items.title: Towards Detecting Neural Audio Codec Synthesized Heart Sounds
items.authors: Girish (UPES; IIIT-Delhi); Orchid Chetia Phukan(NTHU); Mohd Mujtaba Akhtar(VBSPU; IIIT-Delhi); Bhavinkumar Vinodbhai Kuwar(IIIT-Delhi); Swarup Ranjan Behera(Independent Researcher); Arun Balaji Buduru(IIIT-Delhi)
items.abstract: In this paper, we introduce Synthetic Heart Sound Detection (SHAC), a task aimed at identifying phonocardiograms (PCGs) synthesized using neural audio codecs (NACs). To facilitate research in this direction, we release CARDIOFAKE, the first benchmark dataset for SHAC containing both real and codec-synthesized PCGs. We benchmark spectral representations (MFCC, LFCC) and self-supervised learning (SSL) representations (e.g., WavLM) for the task. Furthermore, we propose GROOT, a fusion framework that integrates spectral and SSL features for leveraging their complementary behavior. Experiments show that GROOT, combining MFCC and WavLM, achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming individual representations and competitive baselines.

items.title: Disentangling Speaker Traits for Deepfake Source Verification via Chebyshev Polynomial and Riemannian Metric Learning
items.authors: Xi Xuan(University of Eastern Finland); Wenxin Zhang(University of Chinese Academy of Sciences); Zhiyu Li(University of Science and Technology of China); Jennifer Williams(University of Southampton); Ville Hautamäki(University of Eastern Finland); Tomi Kinnunen(University of Eastern Finland)
items.abstract: Speech deepfake source verification systems aims to determine whether two synthetic speech utterances originate from the same source generator, often assuming that the resulting source embeddings are independent of speaker traits. However, this assumption remains unverified. In this paper, we first investigate the impact of speaker factors on source verification. We propose a speaker-disentangled metric learning (SDML) framework incorporating two novel loss functions. The first leverages Chebyshev polynomial to mitigate gradient instability during disentanglement optimization. The second projects source and speaker embeddings into hyperbolic space, leveraging Riemannian metric distances to reduce speaker information and learn more discriminative source features. Experimental results on MLAAD benchmark, evaluated under four newly proposed protocols designed for source-speaker disentanglement scenarios, demonstrate the effectiveness of SDML framework. The code, evaluation protocols and demo website are available at .

items.title: Interpretable Frequency-Band Attention with Gated SSL Fusion for Audio Deepfake Detection
items.authors: Abeer Alhammad(Thaka); Abdullah Aldahlawi(Thaka)
items.abstract: Synthetic and manipulated speech threatens automatic speaker verification. Self-supervised (SSL) front-ends achieve low error rates but operate as black boxes, revealing little about where in the spectrum spoofing artifacts reside. We propose BandMIL, a band-aware multiple instance learning (MIL) framework that augments SSL representations with interpretable frequency-band analysis. Overlapping windows are split into eight band-specific spectrogram images, encoded by a shared convolutional encoder combined with handcrafted per-band features, and pooled via band attention. Gated fusion adaptively integrates these cues with WavLM representations, and MIL aggregates window predictions into an utterance-level decision without truncation. On ASVspoof 2019 LA, BandMIL achieves 1.28% EER and 0.0331 min t-DCF, improving over SSL-only (1.73% EER). Per-attack analysis shows the band and SSL branches are complementary, while band attention reveals which frequencies drive each decision.

items.title: ArFake: A Robust Framework for Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Spoofing Detection Benchmark
items.authors: Mohamed Elsetohy(MBZUAI); Alhassan Ehab(Queen's University); Ali Mekky(MBZUAI); Besher Hassan(MBZUAI); Shady Shehata(University of Waterloo)
items.abstract: Rapid advances in generative text-to-speech have made it increasingly difficult to distinguish bona fide from synthetic speech, especially for low-resource Arabic dialects, where data scarcity, complex morphology, and non-standard orthography hinder both synthesis and detection. We introduce ARFAKE, the first end-to-end framework for generating and detecting spoofed Arabic speech across eight dialects. The framework generates speech with four TTS models, then assesses quality and intelligibility using classifier-based measures, downstream ASR performance, and human mean opinion scores. We curate a mixed bona fide/synthetic corpus to train a spoofing detector and evaluate robustness both in-domain and under Leave-One-Generator-Out (LOGO) protocols, achieving 96% and 97%. Generalization to unseen dialects is examined with Leave-One-Dialect-Out (LODO) evaluation. ARFAKE establishes a benchmark and a scalable pathway toward stronger Arabic speech security across generators and dialects.

items.title: MSpoofTTS: Multi-Resolution Spoof-Guided Inference for Discrete Speech Synthesis
items.authors: Junchuan Zhao(National University of Singapore); Minh Duc Vu(National University of Singapore); Ye Wang(National University of Singapore)
items.abstract: Neural codec language models enable high-quality discrete speech synthesis, yet their inference remains vulnerable to token-level artifacts and distributional drift that degrade perceptual realism. Rather than relying on preference optimization or retraining, we propose MSpoofTTS, a training-free inference framework that improves zero-shot synthesis through multi-resolution spoof guidance. We introduce a Multi-Resolution Token-based Spoof Detection framework that evaluates codec sequences at different temporal granularities to detect locally inconsistent or unnatural patterns. We then integrate the spoof detectors into a hierarchical decoding strategy, progressively pruning low-quality candidates and re-ranking hypotheses. This discriminator-guided generation enhances robustness without modifying model parameters. Experiments validate the effectiveness of our framework for robust and high-quality codec-based speech generation. Demos are available online.

items.title: MeCo: One-Step MeanFlow-based Corrector for Multi-Channel Speech Separation
items.authors: Dohwan Kim(KAIST); Jung-Woo Choi(KAIST)
items.abstract: While discriminative models for multi-channel speech separation excel in reference-based metrics, they often exhibit suboptimal human listening quality. To address this, we propose a novel MeanFlow-based one-step generative corrector (MeCo). MeCo learns a conditional average velocity field to map discriminative estimates directly onto the clean speech manifold in a single step. To maximize one-step generation performance, we introduce Data-Space Optimization (DSO). DSO integrates an xᵣ-loss, which penalizes prediction errors on longer displacement intervals to serve as a generative objective for human listening quality, with an Endpoint SI-SDR loss that directly optimizes terminal signal fidelity. Experiments demonstrate that MeCo achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with minimal computational overhead, simultaneously achieving superior signal fidelity and human listening quality in both in-domain and out-of-domain scenarios.

items.title: AV-FlowSep: Audio-Visual Target Speaker Separation via Flow Matching
items.authors: Pattara Tipaksorn(NECTEC); Wayupuk Sommuang(Thammasat University); Kwanchiva Thangthai(NECTEC)
items.abstract: This work addresses the task of separating a target speaker's voice from mixtures using visual cues. While existing discriminative approaches achieve strong speech intelligibility, generative diffusion-based methods improve perceptual quality but require many iterative refinement steps. To address these limitations, we propose AV-FlowSep, an audio-visual target speaker separation based on conditional flow matching to learn direct transport paths from mixture to clean mel-spectrogram. We adopt a latent Diffusion Transformer where temporal visual cues from the target speaker are integrated via cross-attention. We demonstrate that AV-FlowSep can generate high perceptual quality with as few as a single inference step. Experiments on VoxCeleb2 and LRS2 across both speech-speech and speech-noise scenarios, show that our approach achieves competitive or superior performance compared to existing baselines, with strong cross-dataset generalization and practical computational efficiency.

items.title: Pseudo-Spatially Conditioned TF-Locoformer with MHCA+FiLM Fusion for Single-Channel Speech Separation
items.authors: Daichi Nitsu(Institute of Science Tokyo); Koichi Shinoda(Institute of Science Tokyo)
items.abstract: Single-channel speech separation in noisy, reverberant environments is challenging as monaural mixtures lack explicit spatial cues. We propose pseudo-spatial conditioning that learns spatially sensitive embeddings from multi-channel training data while using only a single channel at inference. During training, multi-channel mixtures serve as privileged information to pretrain a single-channel encoder with a contrastive triplet objective guided by spatial-configuration differences. This encourages embeddings to reflect spatial configuration rather than speech content. The encoder is jointly fine-tuned with TF-Locoformer to extract pseudo-spatial embeddings. These embeddings condition the separator's time-frequency features via a fusion module combining multi-head cross-attention and feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM). On WHAMR!, SI-SNRi increases from 17.4 to 17.7 dB (S) and from 18.6 to 18.9 dB (M), adding 1.0-1.2M parameters.

items.title: Improving Audio Codec-based Speech Separation By Stacking Residual Vector Quantization Layers
items.authors: Nhu Minh Phuong Dinh(Institute of Science Tokyo); Roland Hartanto(Institute of Science Tokyo); Koichi Shinoda(Institute of Science Tokyo)
items.abstract: Speech separation models trained on raw waveforms achieve high performance but come with substantial computational costs. Neural Audio Codecs (NACs) offer an efficient alternative by operating in compressed latent spaces. However, the existing codec-based method aggregates per-layer Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ) vectors into a single vector, collapsing the coarse-to-fine acoustic hierarchy. We propose RVQ-Grid to explicitly preserve this hierarchy by stacking per-layer RVQ vectors into a 3D grid and processing it using dual-axis recurrent blocks. On WSJ0-2Mix, RVQ-Grid achieves a +3.6 dB SI-SDRi improvement over the prior codec-based method. Our evaluation on the Automatic Speech Recognition task shows that RVQ-Grid achieves an 8.6% WER, demonstrating comparable performance to the SepFormer baseline under the same codec condition. During inference, RVQ-Grid achieves a 6x reduction in MACs compared to SepFormer.

items.title: Speaker Identity as Sole Supervision for Speech Separation
items.authors: Christoph Boeddeker(MERL); Yoshiki Masuyama(Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories (MERL)); Julius Richter(Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories (MERL)); Takahiro Edo(Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories (MERL)); Gordon Wichern(Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories (MERL)); Jonathan Le Roux(Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories (MERL))
items.abstract: Speech separation systems are typically trained with waveform- or spectrogram-level reconstruction losses requiring clean references, spatial cues such as multichannel recordings, or remixing strategies. We investigate whether speech separation can instead be trained using speaker identity as the sole supervision signal. We propose a contrastive objective aligning embeddings of separated outputs with embeddings of auxiliary utterances while repelling competing speakers using in-batch negatives. Unlike target speaker extraction, embeddings are used only to define the training objective and are not required at inference, resulting in a conventional speaker-independent separator. Experiments show that speaker-identity supervision alone can train separation systems from scratch to satisfactory performance and that fine-tuning supervised models on noisy mixtures with this objective further improves separation quality.

items.title: SPOT-TSE: Spatial Point-Guided Target Speech Extraction
items.authors: Taewon Ryu(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University)
items.abstract: Wearable devices such as smart glasses increasingly demand selective listening. Accordingly, recent works often explore region-based spatial target speech extraction (TSE). However, conventional fixed-boundary selection is sensitive to small spatial shifts near boundaries, and methods relying only on distance or azimuth become ambiguous under spatial overlap (e.g., sharing the same distance or azimuth). To address these issues, we propose SPOT-TSE, a multi-channel point-guided TSE framework where the target is specified by a continuous spatial point query in distance and azimuth. We stabilize point-based conditioning via spatial query encoding and proximity-weighted soft targets during training. To further handle overlap cases, we adopt hard-negative spatial sampling. Experiments on simulated smart glasses datasets show improved spatial selectivity and lower word error rate, while reducing computational cost compared to a recurrent baseline.

items.title: Semi-Supervised Joint Separation and Diarization for Multichannel Noisy Speech Mixtures
items.authors: Yuto Nozaki(AIST; Keio University); Kohei Saijo(AIST; Waseda University); Yoshiaki Bando(AIST); Masaki Onishi(AIST)
items.abstract: This paper presents joint separation and diarization for noisy speech mixtures without relying on isolated speech signals. Neural full-rank spatial covariance analysis with speaker activity (FCASA) trains a joint model using only speech mixtures and diarization annotations by incorporating statistical blind source separation. However, because this method largely depends on spatial information, it can be degraded by diffuse noise and result in residual noise in the separated signals. To overcome this limitation, we propose a semi-supervised method that uses clean speech mixtures (e.g., meeting recordings) together with environmental noise recordings. Our method trains noise suppression in a supervised manner while preserving unsupervised separation of speech sources. Both objectives are derived from a unified generative model of multichannel mixtures. Experimental results show that our method improves separation performance over neural FCASA in multiple metrics.

items.title: Don't Listen to Me: A Lightweight, Low-Latency Model for Own-Voice Cancellation in Far-Field Speech Enhancement
items.authors: Mads Østergaard(WS Audiology); Alexander Neergaard Zahid(WS Audiology); Karl Ulbæk(WS Audiology); Andreas Bagge(WS Audiology; Technical University of Denmark); Kenny Falkær Olsen(WS Audiology; Technical University of Denmark); Rasmus Lindrup(Verth)
items.abstract: We introduce own-voice cancellation (OVC): removing a target (enrolled) speaker from a noisy multi-speaker mixture while preserving any remaining speech. Framed as the complement of target speaker extraction, OVC addresses latency-induced own-voice artifacts that arise when a far-field device streams enhanced audio back to the user, as the round-trip time easily exceeds the perceptual threshold for own-voice distortion. We condition a time-domain model with only 2 ms algorithmic latency on a short enrollment utterance and benchmark TD-SpeakerBeam alongside a lighter Mamba-MinGRU masker built from Mamba blocks with MinGRU temporal mixing. Replacing the ConvTasNet-based auxiliary network with a linear RNN encoder improves both signal-to-distortion ratio and predicted MOS while reducing compute. Results establish OVC as a practical, low-latency enhancement objective for far-field denoising.

items.title: Dual-Encoder Fusion with Explicit and Implicit Injection for the Interspeech 2026 Audio Encoder Capability Challenge
items.authors: Yucong Zhang(Wuhan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Zhang Chen(Duke Kunshan University); Juan Liu(Wuhan University); Wei Ju(OPPO); Hongbin Suo(OPPO); Ming Li(The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Wuhan University)
items.abstract: We conduct a systematic study of dual-encoder fusion for the Interspeech 2026 Audio Encoder Capability Challenge (AECC), aiming to translate encoder complementarity into consistent gains across various audio classification and understanding tasks. Using Whisper and Dasheng as complementary encoders, we examine two injection strategies: implicit injection via parameter-efficient Dasheng adaptation before fusion, and explicit injection that decomposes representations into residual components with auxiliary regularization to isolate non-redundant information. Ablations show that explicit injection yields stronger task-wise complementarity and more per-task best results, while implicit adaptation remains competitive and robust overall. We also identify a stable backbone based on token-wise softmax-gated residual fusion with a lightweight STFT residual branch. These results provide practical design insights for modular encoder fusion in the Large Audio Language Model (LALM) framework.

items.title: Balancing Speech Reconstruction and Noise Suppression Using Dual-Asymmetric Loss
items.authors: Merlin Carson(Skyworks Solutions); Suyash Dandekar(Georgia Institute of Technology)
items.abstract: AI-based speech enhancement algorithms are prevalent in speech transmission applications and consumer audio devices. These algorithms typically utilize neural networks to predict filters or masks that attenuate noise in speech signals. However, due to the often-overlapping frequency responses of speech and noise, this process can degrade speech quality or result in residual noise artifacts. In this paper, we present a novel loss function with an adjustable parameter to balance the importance of reconstructing the original speech and the effectiveness of noise suppression. We demonstrate the efficacy of this loss with a variety of state-of-the-art architectures. Experimental results demonstrate improvements over baseline models for the targeted outcome: higher speech quality or enhanced noise suppression. Furthermore, the loss function exhibits a correlation of 0.95 for speech and -0.96 for noise metrics when tested across 13 distinct parameter values.

items.title: SE-AGCNet: An End-to-End Framework for Joint Speech Enhancement and Loudness Control in Meeting Scenarios
items.authors: Jinming Zhang(Zhejiang University); Wei Rao(Nanyang Technological University); Xionghu Zhong(Hunan University); Eng Siong Chng(Nanyang Technological University)
items.abstract: Conventional audio pipelines typically treat speech enhancement (SE) and automatic gain control (AGC) as discrete modules, which often limits overall performance. For instance, applying AGC before SE may inadvertently amplify background noise, while prioritizing SE tends to over-suppress low-volume speech. To address these limitations, we propose SE-AGCNet, an end-to-end framework that jointly optimizes SE and AGC. Tailored for meeting scenarios with significant volume variations, SE-AGCNet leverages the synergy between the two tasks: SE preserves quiet speech, thereby facilitating effective volume adjustment by the AGC component. Furthermore, we propose a specialized data simulation pipeline, SE-AGC-DataGen, and incorporate standardized loudness evaluation metrics: integrated loudness (LUFS), short-term loudness (St LUFS), and LRA. Experiments show that SE-AGCNet consistently achieves target loudness while improving speech quality and ASR accuracy over competitive baselines.

items.title: SLICE: Speech Enhancement via Layer-wise Injection of Conditioning Embeddings
items.authors: Seokhoon Moon(KAIST); Kyudan Jung(KAIST); Jaegul Choo(KAIST)
items.abstract: Real-world speech is often corrupted by multiple degradations simultaneously, including additive noise, reverberation, and nonlinear distortion. Diffusion-based enhancement methods perform well on single degradations but struggle with compound corruptions. Prior noise-aware approaches inject conditioning at the input layer only, which can degrade performance below that of an unconditioned model. To address this, we propose injecting degradation conditioning, derived from a pretrained encoder with multi-task heads for noise type, reverberation, and distortion, into the timestep embedding so that it propagates through all residual blocks without architectural changes. In controlled experiments where only the injection method varies, input-level conditioning performs worse than no encoder at all on compound degradations, while layer-wise injection achieves the best results. The method also generalizes to diverse real-world recordings.

items.title: Neuromorphic Speech Enhancement with Dual-Branch Spiking Neural Networks
items.authors: Taiyu Meng(Hangzhou Dianzi University); Wenbin Jiang(Hangzhou Dianzi University); Haoyi Zhang(Hangzhou Dianzi University); Yuhan Zhou(Hangzhou Dianzi University); Haoyi Yin(Hangzhou Dianzi University)
items.abstract: Spiking neural network (SNN)-based neuromorphic speech enhancement has emerged as a promising paradigm due to its energy efficiency, yet it still underperforms classical artificial neural network (ANN)-based approaches owing to binary activations and the lack of well-designed network architectures. To overcome this limitation, we propose a novel dual-branch spiking neural network architecture equipped with a gated spiking unit (GSU), termed GSU-DBNet. Specifically, GSU-DBNet simultaneously models the speech magnitude spectrum and complex spectrum, predicting the corresponding magnitude and complex spectral masks. Meanwhile, a dual-path GSU module is adopted to exploit temporal and frequency information for enhanced spatiotemporal feature representation. Experiments on a popular benchmark dataset show that GSU-DBNet achieves a PESQ score of 3.04 with only 394K parameters, outperforming existing SNN-based methods while using only 4.5%-10.6% of the parameters of representative ANN-based models.

items.title: Parallel Time-Band Mixing with Learned Observation-Adding for Robust ASR Front-Ends
items.authors: Xingyu Shen(Concordia University; Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology); Runze Wang(Concordia University); Wei-Ping Zhu(Concordia University); Benoit Champagne(McGill University)
items.abstract: Speech enhancement is often used as a front-end for robust ASR, yet recurrent temporal and cross-band modules introduce sequential dependencies that reduce parallel efficiency. In this paper, we present a sequence-parallel band-split enhancement front-end built on a Parallel Time-Band Mixer (PTBM) block that eliminates within-block recurrent unrolling. PTBM integrates intra-band temporal mixing and per-frame cross-band attention within a unified parallel architecture, enabling efficient contextual modeling across both time and frequency dimensions. The system retains the mask-plus-residual reconstruction interface and introduces learned Observation-Adding (LOA) to suppress ASR-sensitive artifacts without development-set tuning. Experiments on DNS Challenge and CHiME-4 with frozen Whisper back-ends show that the proposed front-end consistently reduces word error rate relative to recurrent band-split baselines while requiring only 0.96 M parameters and 0.58 GMAC/s for the front-end network.

items.title: Dictionary-Free Discrete Key-Value Attention for Improving Speech Enhancement
items.authors: Zihao Cui(China Mobile Jiutian Artificial Intelligence Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; Peking University); Jinwei Huang(China Mobile Jiutian Artificial Intelligence Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; Peking University); Tao Li(China Mobile Jiutian Artificial Intelligence Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; Peking University); Rongxiu Zhong(China Mobile Jiutian Artificial Intelligence Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; Peking University); Yingying Gao(China Mobile Jiutian Artificial Intelligence Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; Peking University); Shilei Zhang(China Mobile Jiutian Artificial Intelligence Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; Peking University); Chao Deng(China Mobile Jiutian Artificial Intelligence Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; Peking University); Junlan Feng(China Mobile Jiutian Artificial Intelligence Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.; Peking University)
items.abstract: This paper explores novel attention mechanisms for speech enhancement tasks. Existing Harmonic Attention (HAtt) enhances the reconstructions of the voiced speech spectrum and overall speech quality by constructing a harmonic dictionary. However, HAtt often underperforms on unvoiced components, as its design is constrained by a heavy reliance on prior knowledge for modeling harmonic structures. To address this limitation, we propose a Dictionary-Free Discrete Attention (DFDA) module, which draws inspiration from finite scalar quantization to discretize both keys and values in the attention module in a data-driven manner, thereby learning latent dictionary representations without hand-crafted designs. The HAtt and proposed DFDA are adapted to the TFGridNet block as a new speech enhancement model. Results show this network significantly improves speech quality and intelligibility by effectively suppressing noise and better recovering both voiced and unvoiced spectral structures.

items.title: Time–Frequency Weighted Losses for Phoneme Reconstruction in DNN-Based Speech Enhancement
items.authors: Nasser-Eddine Monir(Université de Lorraine; CNRS; Inria; Loria); Paul Magron(Université de Lorraine; CNRS; Inria; Loria); Romain Serizel(Université de Lorraine; CNRS; Inria; Loria)
items.abstract: Conventional training losses for speech enhancement based on the signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) treat all time-frequency (TF) regions uniformly, overlooking the fine-grained spectral cues that are relevant to specific phoneme intelligibility. We propose a TF weighting framework that modulates the SDR objective based on local speech presence, speech-to-interference ratio (SIR), and spectral flux. By integrating these factors into a differentiable objective, the framework emphasizes TF bins with high speech-noise competition while also accounting for transient cues such as consonant bursts. Experimental results show that our approach improves objective frequency-weighted enhancement metrics, as well as phoneme recognition accuracy, particularly for consonants. Spectral analysis shows better reconstruction of mid-frequency structures at less adverse SIR.

items.title: Bridging the Distribution Gap in Real-World Far-Field Speech Enhancement via Lightweight Latent Representation Alignment
items.authors: Biao Liu(CAS; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences); Haoyuan Xie(CAS; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences); Zengqiang Shang(CAS); Mou Wang(OPPO); Xin Liu(OPPO); Pengyuan Zhang(CAS; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)
items.abstract: Although speech enhancement models have achieved notable progress, their performance degrades in real-world far-field scenarios due to the distribution gap between simulated and real data. To address this problem, we introduce a high-quality real-world dataset. We further propose a lightweight two-stage framework that bridges the distribution gap through latent representation alignment. In the first stage, a pretrained denoising model performs initial noise and reverberation reduction. In the second stage, a distribution mapping module aligns first-stage features to the latent space learned from clean near-field speech, and the decoder reconstructs high-fidelity speech. Experiments on real-world test sets demonstrate that our method effectively suppresses noise while preserving speech structure with only 0.8 GMAC/s computational cost. It achieves 2.94 in P.835 OVRL and 3.35 in P.808, outperforming strong baselines in real-world far-field conditions.

items.title: ARTT: Augmented Reverberant-Target Training for Unsupervised Monaural Speech Dereverberation
items.authors: Siqi Song(Southern University of Science and Technology); Fulin Wu(Southern University of Science and Technology); Zhong-Qiu Wang(Southern University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: Due to the absence of clean reference signals and spatial cues, monaural unsupervised speech dereverberation is a challenging ill-posed inverse problem. To realize it, we propose augmented reverberant-target training (ARTT), which consists of two stages. In the first stage, reverberant-target training (RTT) is proposed to first further reverberate the observed reverberant mixture signal, and then train a deep neural network (DNN) to recover the observed reverberant mixture via discriminative training. Although the target signal to fit is reverberant, we find that the resulting DNN can effectively reduce reverberation. In the second stage, an online self-distillation mechanism based on the mean-teacher algorithm is proposed to further improve dereverberation. Evaluation results demonstrate that ARTT achieves strong unsupervised dereverberation performance, significantly outperforming previous baselines.

items.title: SSL-GMMVC: Interpretable Voice Conversion via Locally Linear GMM Transforms in Self-Supervised Representation Space
items.authors: Tomoya Tanabu(The University of Tokyo); Hiroshi Nishijima(The University of Tokyo); Daisuke Saito(The University of Tokyo); Nobuaki Minematsu(The University of Tokyo)
items.abstract: We introduce SSL-GMMVC, an interpretable voice conversion method in self-supervised speech space. The method models paired source-target features with a Gaussian mixture model and performs conversion as a posterior-weighted sum of affine transforms. This yields locally linear transformations that adapt to heterogeneous feature-space structure while remaining analytically tractable. Through objective and subjective evaluations, we show that SSL-GMMVC improves speaker similarity with comparable intelligibility and naturalness, and that even a constrained covariance variant surpasses a deep learning baseline as the number of mixture components increases. Further analyses link component selection to phonetic structure and reveal interpretable scaling and rotation in the learned transforms. These findings highlight SSL-GMMVC as an effective, analyzable framework for voice conversion.

items.title: From A to B to A: Palindromic Zero-Shot Voice Conversion with Non-Parallel Data
items.authors: Moshe Mandel(Independent); Shlomi E. Chazan(OriginAI)
items.abstract: We present a voice conversion (VC) framework that utilizes K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) retrieval over WavLM representations to align non-parallel source and target speech, constructing synthetic training pairs for supervised learning. The retrieved segments serve as synthetic inputs, while real target audio provides ground-truth outputs, forming a synthetic-to-real training paradigm that naturally supports multilingual data without requiring parallel corpora or explicit alignment. To ensure consistent target-speaker identity, we incorporate a speaker loss derived from a pretrained speaker verification model. Experiments across multiple languages demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high naturalness and strong speaker similarity, outperforming competitive VC baselines, despite being trained exclusively on English data. Samples can be accessed at: https://palindromic-vc.github.io.

items.title: MeanVoiceFlow2: Joint Optimization of Mean Flow and Content Encoder for Fast One-Step Zero-Shot Voice Conversion
items.authors: Takuhiro Kaneko(NTT, Inc.); Hirokazu Kameoka(NTT, Inc.); Kou Tanaka(NTT, Inc.); Yuto Kondo(NTT, Inc.)
items.abstract: Flow-matching approaches to voice conversion (VC) have gained attention owing to their high speech quality and strong speaker similarity. Among them, one-step models such as MeanVoiceFlow are particularly attractive because they enable efficient inference; however, their reliance on a computationally intensive content encoder remains a bottleneck. We therefore propose MeanVoiceFlow2, a framework that jointly optimizes a flow-based conversion module and a computationally efficient content encoder. The model is trained through conversion distillation using MeanVoiceFlow and the reconstruction of real data. We further incorporate diffusion-GAN training with sample mixing and teacher-guided conditioning augmentation to enhance realism and disentanglement. Experiments on zero-shot VC showed that MeanVoiceFlow2 achieved higher perceptual quality and approximately 9× faster inference than MeanVoiceFlow while maintaining comparable speaker similarity.

items.title: Zero-VC: Zero-Lookahead Streaming Voice Conversion via Speaker Anonymization
items.authors: Yudong Li(The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen Loop Area Institute); Zihao Fang(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Junwen Qiu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Ruihai Jing(Shenzhen Transsion Holdings Co., Ltd.); Ruixiang Hang(Shenzhen Transsion Holdings Co., Ltd.); Yingda Shen(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Zhizheng Wu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen Loop Area Institute; Amphion Technology Co.,Ltd.)
items.abstract: Streaming zero-shot voice conversion struggles to disentangle timbre from linguistic content without degrading utility or inflating latency. Current methods rely on information bottleneck (IB) or speaker perturbation. While IB filters out timbre, it discards prosody, forcing models to explicitly inject features like fundamental frequency. This often requires buffering future frames, creating algorithmic lookahead latency. On the other hand, existing perturbation methods largely overlook the crucial trade-off between timbre leakage and utility preservation. Recognizing this neglected trade-off, we find that the inherent objective of Speaker Anonymization (SA) aligns well with balancing these factors. Thus, we introduce SA as a novel perturbation mechanism to explicitly mitigate timbre leakage while retaining prosodic utility. Crucially, SA's robust representations significantly alleviate the generator's reliance on future context, enabling our strictly causal, zero-lookahead network.

items.title: Improving Model Expressivity and Speaker Matching in Low-Latency Voice Conversion
items.authors: Anders R. Bargum(Aalborg University); Simon Lajboschitz(Khora & Heka VR); Stefania Serafin(Technical University of Denmark); Cumhur Erkut(Aalborg University)
items.abstract: Real-time voice conversion systems struggle to achieve high speaker similarity in zero-shot scenarios, especially under lightweight computational constraints. This challenge stems from a lack of model expressivity and the difficulty of capturing comprehensive speaker-relevant information within the strict latency requirements. We propose a real-time voice conversion framework that addresses this limitation by adding lost prosody explicitly through an excitation signal and by fusing complementary information into the conventional global speaker embeddings. To ensure robust feature disentanglement, we furthermore employ an encoder-specific information perturbation strategy during training. Our approach maintains causal inference requirements and preserves prosodic and linguistic content while operating under low-latency constraints. Experimental evaluations demonstrate improvements in speaker-matching metrics over state-of-the-art real-time baselines.

items.title: Universal Speech Content Factorization
items.authors: Henry Li Xinyuan(Johns Hopkins University); Zexin Cai(Johns Hopkins University); Lin Zhang(Johns Hopkins University); Paola Garcia-Perera(Johns Hopkins University); Berrak Sisman(Johns Hopkins University); Sanjeev Khudanpur(Johns Hopkins University); Nicholas Andrews(Johns Hopkins University); Matthew Wiesner(Johns Hopkins University)
items.abstract: We propose Universal Speech Content Factorization (USCF), a simple and invertible linear method for extracting a low-rank speech representation in which speaker timbre is suppressed while phonetic content is preserved. USCF extends Speech Content Factorization, a closed-set voice conversion (VC) method, to an open-set setting by learning a universal speech-to-content mapping via least-squares optimization and deriving speaker-specific transformations from only a few seconds of target speech. We show through embedding analysis that USCF effectively removes speaker-dependent variation. As a zero-shot VC system, USCF achieves competitive intelligibility, naturalness, and speaker similarity compared to methods that require substantially more target-speaker data or additional neural training. Finally, we demonstrate that as a training-efficient timbre-disentangled speech feature, USCF features can serve as the acoustic representation for training timbre-prompted text-to-speech models. Speech samples and code are publicly available.

items.title: CFLOW-VC: An unsupervised cycle training strategy based on normalizing flows for Voice Conversion
items.authors: FeiBao Song(Anhui Univeristy)
items.abstract: Voice conversion (VC) aims to transfer the timbre of a target speaker while preserving the content of a source speech. A key challenge, especially in non-parallel settings, is the train-test mismatch: during training, models often learn from utterances where content and timbre are from the same speaker, hindering their ability to disentangle these factors effectively during inference. In this work, we propose CFLOW-VC, an unsupervised cycle training strategy based on normalizing flows, built upon the end-to-end VITS framework for high-fidelity waveform generation. We introduce a mel-style encoder to capture expressive style features and employ data augmentation to improve robustness in noisy environments. Experimental results demonstrate that CFLOW-VC outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both objective and subjective evaluations. Audio samples are publicly available.

items.title: WhispEar: A Bidirectional Framework for Scaling Whispered Speech Conversion via Pseudo-Parallel Whisper Generation
items.authors: Zihao Fang(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Yingda Shen(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Zifan Guan(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Tongtong Song(Honor Device Co., Ltd); Zhenyi Liu(Honor Device Co., Ltd); Zhizheng Wu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen Research Institute of Big Data; Shenzhen Loop Area Institute; Amphion Technology Co., Ltd.)
items.abstract: Whispered speech lacks vocal fold vibration and fundamental frequency, resulting in degraded acoustic cues and making whisper-to-normal (W2N) conversion challenging, especially with limited parallel data. We propose WhispEar, a bidirectional framework based on unified semantic representations that capture speaking-mode-invariant information shared by whispered and normal speech. The framework contains both W2N and normal-to-whisper (N2W) models. Notably, the N2W model enables zero-shot pseudo-parallel whisper generation from abundant normal speech, allowing scalable data augmentation for W2N training. Increasing generated data consistently improves performance. We also release the largest bilingual (Chinese-English) whispered-normal parallel corpus to date. Experiments demonstrate that WhispEar outperforms strong baselines and benefits significantly from scalable pseudo-parallel data.

items.title: Imitation Learning for Elder-Facing Speech Synthesis
items.authors: Dongrui Han(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Weidong Chen(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Jiawen Kang(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Mingyu Cui(Tencent Hunyuan); Helen Meng(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Xixin Wu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Recent advances in text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis have achieved highly natural and expressive speech generation. However, these systems are designed for general adults and overlook older adults' speech comprehension needs due to age-related sensory and cognitive decline. Prior work involves older adults by collecting preference feedback to tune model parameters. However, obtaining sufficient preference data is costly and difficult, as older adults quickly become fatigued during collection. In this paper, we propose a novel imitation learning (IL) framework to learn TTS models from expert demonstrations. We further improve Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with two-stage on-policy reward learning (OPRL) to mitigate reward hacking under limited supervision from expert demonstration. Experimental results show that GRPO w/ OPRL outperforms GRPO and supervised baselines in objective and subjective metrics. Audio samples are available at https://dongru1.github.io/demo/im-efss/

items.title: How Linguistic Dimension Interactions Shape Meaning Preservation in Multilingual ASR
items.authors: Simon Gonzalez(DSTG); Tao Hoang(DSTG); Bradley Donnelly(DSTG); Jason Littlefield(DSTG); Myung Kim(DSTG); Chloe Dean(DSTG); Jennifer Biggs(DSTG); Hayden Ooi(DSTG); Latchman Singh(DSTG); Tim Cawley(DSTG)
items.abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition errors emerge from interactions across linguistic dimensions. While prior work correlated errors with external features, it remains unclear whether these patterns hold when linguistic features are measured from ASR outputs. We analysed substitution errors on the FLEURS dataset using Whisper and Seamless, computing phonetic, morphological, syntactic, and lexical similarity directly from ASR audio and transcriptions. Results revealed that semantic preservation emerges from systematic cross-dimension interactions: morphological and syntactic features operated interdependently while phonological accuracy intensified when syntax was preserved. Interaction patterns differed across architectures: Seamless showed better baseline performance, while Whisper showed heightened error sensitivity but leveraged morphological information more effectively, showing that ASR architectures integrate linguistic information through fundamentally different mechanisms.

items.title: Language-Aware Distillation for Multilingual Instruction-Following Speech LLMs with ASR-Only Supervision
items.authors: Shreyas Gopal(Nanyang Technological University); Donghang Wu(Nanyang Technological University; National University of Singapore); Ashutosh Anshul(Nanyang Technological University); Yeo Yue Heng(Nanyang Technological University; A*STAR); Yizhou Peng(Nanyang Technological University); Haoyang Li(Nanyang Technological University); Hexin Liu(Nanyang Technological University); Eng Siong Chng(Nanyang Technological University)
items.abstract: Speech Large Language Models (LLMs) that understand and follow instructions in many languages are useful for real-world interaction, but are difficult to train with supervised fine-tuning, requiring large, task-specific speech corpora. While recent distillation-based approaches train performant English-only Speech LLMs using only annotated ASR data by aligning text and speech using only a lightweight projector, these models under-perform when scaled to multilingual settings due to language interference in the shared projector. We address this by introducing language-aware distillation using a query bank and a gating network that selects or mixes query tokens using a Q-Former projector. Our approach shows gains of 14% over matched multilingual distillation baselines on instruction following. We further synthesize Audio-MLQA, a multilingual spoken QA benchmark built on MLQA with high-quality TTS questions. Our best model improves over existing Speech LLM baselines by 32% on Audio-MLQA.

items.title: ERM-MinMaxGAP: Benchmarking and Mitigating Gender Bias in Multilingual Multimodal Speech-LLM Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Zi Haur Pang(Kyoto University); Xiaoxue Gao(A*STAR); Tatsuya Kawahara(Kyoto University); Nancy Chen(A*STAR)
items.abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) systems can exhibit gender-related performance disparities, but how such bias manifests in multilingual speech LLMs across languages and modalities is unclear. We introduce a novel multilingual, multimodal benchmark built on MELD-ST, spanning English, Japanese, and German, to quantify language-specific SER performance and gender gaps. We find bias is strongly language-dependent, and multimodal fusion does not reliably improve fairness. To address these, we propose ERM-MinMaxGAP, a fairness-informed training objective, which augments empirical risk minimization (ERM) with a proposed adaptive fairness weight mechanism and a novel MinMaxGAP regularizer on the maximum male-female loss gap within each language and modality. Building upon the Qwen2-Audio backbone, our ERM-MinMaxGAP approach improves multilingual SER performance by 5.5% and 5.0% while reducing the overall gender bias gap by 0.1% and 1.4% in the unimodal and multimodal settings, respectively.

items.title: Confidence-Gated Mean-Teacher Consistency Regularization for Low-Resource Multilingual ASR with Shared–Private Fusion-LoRA
items.authors: Jie Liu(Xinjiang University); Liang He(Xinjiang University; Tsinghua University); Longwei Li(Xinjiang University); Qingyuan Ma(Xinjiang University); Xuejian Zhao(Xinjiang University)
items.abstract: Low-resource multilingual ASR commonly relies on joint training, but excessive parameter sharing can cause negative transfer. Meanwhile, consistency learning as a remedy for limited labels may amplify cross-view instability and confirmation bias when predictions are unreliable. To tackle this, we propose a Whisper-based parameter-efficient framework. Architecturally, it adopts a shared-private Fusion-LoRA design (SPF-LoRA): a shared branch learns cross-lingual commonality, a private branch captures language-specific traits, and a learnable fusion weight adaptively balances both to mitigate multilingual interference. In training, we introduce a Mean-Teacher consistency regularization strategy (MT-CR), where an EMA teacher provides more stable consistency targets and reliability filtering suppresses noisy consistency signals. On Kathbath, we reduce macro WER by 35.4% over Whisper-small+LoRA, outperform the reported Whisper-medium+LoRA baseline, and improve all five languages.

items.title: Speech Encoder Fusion for LLM-based Automatic Speech Recognition
items.authors: Jakob Poncelet(KU Leuven); Hugo Van hamme(KU Leuven)
items.abstract: Speech-aware large language models (LLMs) can incorporate speech through pre-trained acoustic encoders that project speech features into the LLM embedding space. While the choice of the speech encoder critically influences performance, different encoders often exhibit complementary strengths, motivating their combination. In this work, we investigate whether fusing multiple pre-trained speech encoders can enhance speech-aware LLMs for automatic speech recognition (ASR). We explore several fusion strategies beyond simple feature concatenation, including learned combinations and Transformer-based fusion architectures, and evaluate them across mono- and multilingual ASR settings as well as diarized speech recognition. Our results indicate that carefully fusing multiple parallel speech encoders improves downstream performance in all scenarios with limited computational overhead.

items.title: Dissecting Sensitivity to Training Language in Self-Supervised Speech Learning Using Neural Audio Codec Tokens
items.authors: Daigo Takizawa(National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology); Tomohiko Nakamura(National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology); Samuele Cornell(Carnegie Mellon University); William Chen(Carnegie Mellon University); Satoru Fukayama(National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology); Shinji Watanabe(Carnegie Mellon University)
items.abstract: Neural audio codecs (NACs) have become popular for obtaining speech representations as discrete tokens. Beyond compression, discrete tokens can be used to train self-supervised learning (SSL) models. Such models, referred to as codec-based SSL models, reduce data storage and computational cost, enabling scalable SSL pre-training. However, their language sensitivity remains unclear. When the language changes, codec-based SSL models may require retraining, which undermines their efficiency. In this paper, we present a systematic analysis of language sensitivity by varying either the NAC training language or the SSL pre-training language while keeping the other fixed. Experimental results show that downstream performance is insensitive to the NAC training language but strongly dependent on the SSL pre-training language. These findings suggest that a single NAC can be reused across languages, while aligning the SSL pre-training language with the target language is crucial.

items.title: SᴜTRA: Structurally-Unified Tokenization with Root Awareness
items.authors: Vaibhav Rathore(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.; Indian Institute of Technology); Siddhant Gole(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.; Indian Institute of Technology); Dadhichi Telwadkar(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.); Rooshil Bhatia(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.); Maulik Ruparel(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.); Siddharth Surekha(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.); Neha Bhargava(Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.)
items.abstract: Existing subword tokenizers optimize statistical compression but ignore morphological structure, particularly the relationship between roots and affixes. This is harmful for morphologically rich Indic languages, where basic units are complex orthographic syllables (aksharas) rather than letters. Frequency-based methods over-fragment words, arbitrarily splitting roots and affixes—a phenomenon we term Morphological Shattering. We propose SᴜTRA (Structurally-Unified Tokenization with Root Awareness), a morphology-aware algorithm that preserves akshara indivisibility and penalizes merges crossing morphological boundaries. We also release a new morphological segmentation dataset for Hindi, Marathi, and Gujarati. SᴜTRA reduces shattering, achieving peak gains of +14.7% in morphological alignment (Boundary F1) and +34% in semantic recoverability (Hindi) over Bᴘᴇ. These structural gains yield an average improvement of +8.08 ᴄʜʀF2 in machine translation.

items.title: Measuring the Redundancy of Decoder Layers in SpeechLLMs
items.authors: Adel Moumen(University of Cambridge); Guangzhi Sun(University of Cambridge); Philip C Woodland(University of Cambridge)
items.abstract: Speech Large Language Models route speech encoder representations into an LLM decoder that typically accounts for over 90% of total parameters. We study how much of this decoder capacity is actually needed for speech tasks. Across two LLM families and three scales (1-8B), we show that decoder redundancy is largely inherited from the pretrained LLM: text and speech inputs yield similar redundant blocks. We then measure excess capacity by pruning decoder layers and analysing post-pruning healing to increase robustness. Our findings show that 7-8B models retain good ASR performance with only ~60% of decoder layers, and the same trend extends to smaller scales with reduced pruning tolerance. We then generalise to speech translation, and show that the same blocks of layers are redundant across speech encoders, tasks and languages, indicating that a more global redundancy structure exists, enabling a single pruned SpeechLLM backbone to support multiple tasks at lower computational cost.

items.title: Weakly Masked Residual Reliability Learning for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Speech Models
items.authors: Yuan Li(Inner Mongolia University); Yonghe Wang(Inner Mongolia University); Zhenjie Gao(Inner Mongolia University); Feilong Bao(Inner Mongolia University); Xiaodong Yang(National Computer Network Emergency Response Technical Team Coordination Center); Bo Pang(National Computer Network Emergency Response Technical Team Coordination Center); Yandong Guo(National Computer Network Emergency Response Technical Team Coordination Center)
items.abstract: This paper proposes a Weakly Masked Residual Reliability Learning (WMR2L) framework to enhance the robustness of speech models in cross-domain scenarios. WMR2L jointly models prediction confidence and residual dispersion for pseudo-label weighting, enabling the separation of reliable predictions from overconfident ones. To mitigate supervision bias introduced by selective pseudo-labeling, we propose a weak confidence masking strategy that partially masks high-confidence regions, thereby promoting learning from less reliable regions. In addition, a multi-perturbation consistency regularization is designed to further improve pseudo-label quality. Experimental results show that WMR2L consistently outperforms existing baselines across multiple cross-domain speech recognition tasks, achieving relative WER reductions of 13.8% on CHiME-4 (noisy), 25.0% on SLURP (human-machine interaction), and 15.7% on CORAAL (accented), and also yields notable improvements on speech translation tasks. Our code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/ status/Speech-Model-Adaptation-8D45

items.title: Contrastive Training with LLM-generated Near-Misses for Robust Code-Switching Speech Recognition
items.authors: Tung X. Nguyen(VinUniversity); Hieu Minh Truong(VinUniversity); Giang Son Nguyen(VinUniversity); Nhu Vo(VinUniversity; University of Technology Sydney); Wray Buntine(VinUniversity; Monash University); Dung D. Le(VinUniversity)
items.abstract: Code-switching (CS), the alternation between multiple languages within a single utterance, remains challenging for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR). To address this issue, we propose a Point-of-Interest (POI)-aware contrastive training framework that improves recognition at CS-critical regions. We first identify CS spans by adopting POI detection method from literature, then construct acoustically plausible near-miss hypotheses by perturbing POIs in ASR N-best outputs and expanding candidates with a large language model. Hard but plausible negatives are retained through filtering with acoustic, phonemic, and textual constraints. Finally, we fine-tune Whisper-small with LoRA using a POI-weighted cross-entropy anchor objective together with a multi-negative contrastive ranking loss. Experiments on CS-FLEURS (cmn-eng) and ViMedCSS (vie-eng) show consistent reductions of over 2% in both general and CS-aware error rates compared to standard LoRA fine-tuning.

items.title: L-Proto: Language-Aware Episodic Prototypical Training for Multilingual Speaker Verification
items.authors: Hyung-Seok Oh(Korea University); Deok-Hyeon Cho(Korea University); Seung-Bin Kim(Korea University); Seong-Whan Lee(Korea University)
items.abstract: Multilingual speaker verification remains challenging because language-dependent acoustic variability causes speaker identity to become entangled with linguistic characteristics, degrading generalization across languages. In multilingual training, embeddings often encode language cues with speaker identity, causing speakers to form language-specific clusters. We propose L-Proto, a language-aware episodic prototypical training strategy that constructs language-consistent episodes. By sampling speakers from a single language per episode, L-Proto reduces language-driven variation during training and encourages embeddings to focus more directly on speaker identity. Experiments on the TidyVoice Challenge benchmark demonstrate consistent performance improvements over conventional fine-tuning and random episodic sampling across multiple backbone architectures.

items.title: Progressive Learning for Robust Speaker Representation
items.authors: Nikhil Keetha(Meeami Technologies); Hima Jyothi R(Meeami Technologies); Nivedita Chennupati(Meeami Technologies); Balaji Padmanaban(Meeami Technologies); Harish Rajamani(Meeami Technologies); Naveen Ambati(Meeami Technologies)
items.abstract: Speaker embeddings are foundational to voice technologies like speaker verification, diarization and target speaker extraction. The embeddings must remain robust to environmental noise and invariant to spoken language. In this paper, we propose a speaker embedding model based on the ReDimNet architecture, which has shown state-of-the-art performance on Voxceleb. To improve the robustness of speaker embeddings under cross-lingual and diverse acoustic conditions, model is trained on a large-scale multilingual corpus with extensive noise and reverb augmentation. Further, a post-network is trained with triplet loss to disentangle speaker identity from linguistic content, thereby encouraging language-invariant representations. The proposed model is evaluated on the TidyVoice Challenge dataset. Under the matched and mismatched language scenarios, Our model achieves an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 1.58%, demonstrating strong robustness to both noise and language variability.

items.title: Orthogonal Feature Projection and Manifold-Constrained Neural PLDA for the TidyVoice2026 Cross-Lingual Speaker Verification Challenge
items.authors: Yuxuan Du(Beijing Fosafer Information Technology Co.,Ltd.); Xing He(University of Electronic Science and Technology of China); Jingwen Yang(Beijing Fosafer Information Technology Co.,Ltd.); Xupeng Jia(Beijing Fosafer Information Technology Co.,Ltd.); Yankai Wang(Beijing Fosafer Information Technology Co.,Ltd.); Weili Jiang(Ministry of Public Security); Kai Gao(Ministry of Public Security); Boyu Zhao(Ministry of Public Security); Rong Zheng(Beijing Fosafer Information Technology Co.,Ltd.); Jing Deng(Beijing Fosafer Information Technology Co.,Ltd.)
items.abstract: This paper presents the Fosafer team's system developed for the TidyVoice2026 Cross-lingual Speaker Verification Challenge. To mitigate the over-reliance of current models on language-specific features, we propose a robust system based on orthogonal feature projection and manifold-constrained neural Probabilistic Linear Discriminant Analysis (PLDA). For front-end feature extraction, orthogonal projection decouples redundant self-supervised features and dynamically integrates language-agnostic components into speaker embeddings. For back-end scoring, we employ a manifold-constrained neural PLDA to perform discriminative optimization while adhering to probabilistic generative constraints. To optimize PLDA training, we design a dynamic hard sample mining strategy for multilingual scenarios. Our final fused system achieved equal error rates (EERs) of 1.39% and 1.95% on the two test tracks, respectively, securing 1st place among 42 participating teams.

items.title: LaS-LCA: Layer-Selected Latent Cross-Attention Adapters and Margin-Mixup for Robust Cross-Lingual Speaker Verification
items.authors: Xu Shen(Waseda University); Yihao Zhao(Waseda University); Xinwei Wu(Wuhan University); Hao Liang(Waseda University); Yujie Zhu(Wuhan University); Yujin Wang(Wuhan University); Wei Liu(Wuhan University; Waseda University); Gongping Huang(Wuhan University); Shoji Makino(Waseda University)
items.abstract: Cross-lingual speaker verification suffers from significant performance degradation due to language mismatch. To effectively maintain stable speaker recognition across diverse languages, we propose layer-selected latent cross-attention adapters (LaS-LCA), a novel framework designed to adapt frozen large-scale pre-trained models. Specifically, we strategically select backbone layers to isolate speaker traits from linguistic noise. Within the adapter, shared latent cross-attention and convolutional modeling distill multi-layer features into a consistent, language-independent latent space. To further mitigate overfitting on limited cross-lingual data, we additionally incorporate an embedding-level margin-mixup strategy during the training phase. Experimental results on the TidyVoiceX benchmark demonstrate that LaS-LCA achieves an EER of 1.40%, significantly outperforming baseline models and exhibiting superior robustness across diverse linguistic conditions.

items.title: Dual-LoRA: Parameter-Efficient Adversarial Disentanglement for Cross-Lingual Speaker Verification
items.authors: Qituan Shangguan(Nanjing University); Junhao Du(Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Jiangsu Key Lab); Kunyang Peng(AISpeech; Jiangsu Key Lab); Feng Xue(AISpeech; Jiangsu Key Lab); Hui Zhang(AISpeech; Jiangsu Key Lab); Xinsheng Wang(Soul AI Lab); Kai Yu(Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Jiangsu Key Lab); Shuai Wang(Nanjing University)
items.abstract: Cross-lingual speaker verification suffers from severe language-speaker entanglement. This causes systematic degradation in the hardest scenario: correctly accepting utterances from the same speaker across different languages while rejecting those from different speakers sharing the same language. Standard adversarial disentanglement degrades speaker discriminability; blind discriminators inadvertently penalize speaker-discriminative traits that merely correlate with language. To address this, we propose Dual-LoRA, injecting trainable task-factorized LoRA adapters into a frozen pre-trained backbone. Our core innovation is a Language-Anchored Adversary: by grounding the discriminator with an explicit language branch, adversarial gradients target true linguistic cues rather than arbitrary correlations, preserving essential speaker characteristics. Evaluated on the TidyVoice benchmark, our system achieves a 0.91% validation EER and ranks 3rd in the official challenge.

items.title: Cross-Lingual Speaker Verification with Self-Supervised Pre-Trained Models
items.authors: Jinghan Peng(Ant Group); Yu Zheng(Ant Group); Weiqiang Wang(Ant Group); Jian Liu(Ant Group)
items.abstract: Speaker verification (SV) performance degrades under language mismatch due to the entanglement of speaker identity with language-specific acoustic cues. To address this problem, we leverage large-scale self-supervised pre-trained models (PTMs) to learn language-agnostic speaker representations. We utilize PTMs as robust front-end feature extractors, capitalizing on their rich acoustic and linguistic knowledge acquired from vast, diverse audio data. These generalized features are then used to train a downstream speaker embedding network, effectively disentangling speaker identity from language-specific characteristics. We validate our approach on the TidyVoice2026 benchmark, which benchmarks SV under language mismatch. Our proposed system (team T02) achieves equal error rates (EERs) of 2.21% on tv26_eval-A and 2.99% on tv26_eval-U.

items.title: Language-Invariant Multilingual Speaker Verification for the TidyVoice 2026 Challenge
items.authors: Ze Li(Wuhan University; Duke Kunshan University); Xiaoxiao Miao(Duke Kunshan University); Juan Liu(Wuhan University); Ming Li(The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen; Wuhan University)
items.abstract: Multilingual speaker verification (SV) remains challenging due to limited cross-lingual data and language-dependent information in speaker embeddings. This paper presents a languageinvariant multilingual SV system for the TidyVoice 2026 Challenge. We adopt the multilingual self-supervised w2v-BERT 2.0 model as the backbone, enhanced with Layer Adapters and Multi-scale Feature Aggregation to better exploit multilayer representations. A language-adversarial training strategy with a Gradient Reversal Layer is applied to promote language-invariant speaker embeddings. Moreover, a multilingual zero-shot text-to-speech system is used to synthesize speech in multiple languages, improving language diversity. Experimental results demonstrate that fine-tuning the large-scale pretrained model yields competitive performance, while language-adversarial training further enhances robustness. In addition, synthetic speech augmentation provides additional gains under limited training data conditions. Source code is available at https://github.com/ZXHY-82/LI-MSV-TidyVoice2026.

items.title: Effectiveness of Language Variability Compensation in Speaker Verification
items.authors: Ladislav Mošner(Brno University of Technology); Sara Barahona(Universidad Autónoma de Madrid); Sandro Cumani(Politecnico di Torino); Johan Rohdin(Brno University of Technology); Jin Li(Brno University of Technology; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Oldřich Plchot(Brno University of Technology)
items.abstract: We present our submission to the TidyVoice 2026 Challenge along with a systematic study of language-variability compensation across the entire speaker verification pipeline. We investigate multilingual fine-tuning and language compensation techniques at the embedding, back-end, and score levels. Each approach independently yields consistent, comparable gains, confirming that explicitly addressing language effects is crucial. We further show that powerful back-ends such as PSVM and SG-TPSDA perform strongly with language-entangled embeddings, but their advantage decreases when language variability is mitigated at the front-end via adversarial training with gradient reversal. Our submitted system achieves 2.53% EER on tv26_eval-A.
